newsitem.title: MEXICO: Hernan downgraded to tropical storm from hurricane.
newsitem.headline: Hernan downgraded to tropical storm from hurricane.

text.p: Hurricane Hernan was downgraded to a tropical storm on Thursday after hitting land over the western Mexican state of Jalisco, but authorities remained on alert, a state Civil Protection Unit spokesman said.
"We are in a state of alert," spokesman Luis Antonio del Castillo said. "There has been a lot of rain but as of the moment we don't have any deaths or injuries or structural damage."
Hernan was packing winds of 53 mph (85 kph) with gusts of up to 62 mph (100 kph) as it moved northeast over land, del Castillo said.

A Commnications and Transportation Ministry bulletin said the storm generated waves of more than 12 feet (four meters), causing the ministry to close three ports: Manzanillo in Colima state, Lazaro Cardenas in Michoacan and Puerto Vallarta in Jalisco.
Lazardo Cardenas was closed on Wednesday. Manzanillo was closed on Tuesday but was reopened for a time Wednesday. Puerto Vallarta had not previously been closed.
